Interesting. I'd love to know what Microsoft's long term plan and vision are. They seem to be struggling to find a foothold in the mobile market and even their desktop monopoly seems to be more volatile than ever. Well here's to hoping they eventually port of Visual Studio in its entirety. That piece of software is the one thing keeping me from swapping to linux as my primary OS.
Have you tried Mono? Mono is an open source implementation of Microsoft's .NET Framework based on the ECMA standards for C# and the Common Language Runtime.

Mono is an implementation of a language. Visual Studio is the tool you use to develop in the language. Think of it more like English and MS Word respectively. I'd be developing using Mono, but I'm not particularly fond of the IDEs / integrated development environments currently natively available on Linux.
You have Eclipse, NetBeans and cloud-based tools as well. Although I am only familiar with Mono and Netbeans at the moment.
There's Xamarin. It's what you use to develop for mono. It's got similarities to Visual Studio. It's mostly cost-free, though you have to pay to develop for Android and iOS.

I played around with this for short bit and it's pretty awesome so far! It supports Emmet and Git out of the box as well as SCSS, Dockerfiles, Handlebars and every language I may happen to use. As it is now, I think I might be comfortable switching to it from Atom, but I'm interested in how plugin and theme support will work. The defaults are quite nice though.
